stemBlocks.value: K, L, M and N lie on a circle with centre O, and XY is a tangent to the circle at K. In the diagram the tangent–chord angle to KN is 56° (marked between KX and KN), angle MKO = 12° and angle LKY = 48°. (i) Find angle KOL, giving reasons for each step. (ii)(b) Find angle LMN.
Think first: Two radii to the ends of a chord always make an isosceles triangle — that is the route to an angle at the centre.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p251-q15 from workbook page 251.

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the right angle between the tangent and the radius OK.

contentBlocks.value: ∠OKY = 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius at the point of contact), so ∠OKL = 90 − 48

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the isosceles triangle formed by the two radii.

contentBlocks.value: OK = OL (radii of the same circle), so ∠OLK = ∠OKL = 42°

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply the angle sum of triangle KOL.
Find angle NKL from the angles on the straight tangent line XKY.
Use the cyclic quadrilateral KNML, in which K and M are opposite vertices.

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract the 48° from the tangent–radius right angle to get angle OKL, use OK = OL to get the other base angle, then find angle KOL; for angle LMN use the angles on the straight tangent line at K and the cyclic quadrilateral KNML.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) ∠KOL = 96°: the tangent is perpendicular to the radius OK, so ∠OKL = 90° − 48° = 42°; OK = OL are radii, so ∠OLK = 42°; the angle sum of triangle KOL then gives 180 − 42 − 42 = 96°.  (ii)(b) ∠LMN = 104°: the angles on the straight line XKY give ∠NKL = 180 − 56 − 48 = 76°, and KNML is a cyclic quadrilateral, so ∠LMN = 180 − 76 = 104°. (A check: the tangent–chord angle of 48° gives ∠KNL = 48°, so the centre angle ∠KOL = 96° as found.)

whyThisWorks.value: Every radius meets the tangent at 90°, so angles measured from the tangent can always be converted into angles measured from a radius. Because two radii to the same chord are equal, the triangle they form is isosceles and its apex angle at the centre follows from the angle sum. The angles at K along the tangent line add to a straight angle, giving the interior angle of the cyclic quadrilateral, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Treating ∠OKL as 48° instead of 90° − 48°.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting that OK = OL makes triangle KOL isosceles and assuming it is equilateral or right-angled.

examTip.value: Draw in the radii to both ends of a chord whenever a centre angle is wanted — the isosceles triangle is nearly always the quickest route.
